selection: Ordinary selectors require ten entered trades/eight contracts, positive return at both 5% and 10% costs and the training drawdown ceiling; maximize 10%-cost return. Robust selectors require fourteen trades/ten contracts/three trading days and positive 10%-cost return after excluding two best contracts by aggregate PnL and after excluding the best entry day. Cash is allowed. The last fit uses the full old dataset and adds no evaluation day.
execution: One open position. Compare one purchase per token, up to two or three purchases, a 120-second cooldown, and re-entry only after a profitable or losing completed position. Limits persist across evaluation days. Prior result means actual entered-trade PnL after modeled costs. $1,000 account, 1% of pre-call economic volume, five-second indexing lag, five prior swaps and twice prior median gas/MEV fees. Entries and exits are delayed market fills; a missing exit is written off.
design: Reuse exactly the sender-based shortlist produced before each cutoff, including all its exit/delay/sizing/re-entry policies. Recompute every training portfolio once with sender history and once with checked requester history. Apply identical selection rules independently. This isolates attribution within an identical candidate pool; it does not search requester-specific candidates outside that original shortlist. Actual human/bot signal filters remain unchanged.
scope: Previously examined dates, not new independent evidence. Original-text availability and later corroboration of reply metadata restrict the sample. Baseline ledgers must reproduce exactly. Also change attribution with original choices fixed, and remove attribution from requester-fitted choices.
